correspondence.finding: The selected opening makes a westward hook before turning northeast toward the upper Mineurs corridor. The reserve-management map includes the general headwater terrain, small waters and forest mosaics, but the channel around the opening is not continuously distinguishable from sector boundaries and thematic symbols. The thesis detailed survey figure begins farther downstream. The actual opening and any small-water or wetland passage into the identified upper Mineurs remain unestablished.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The long northeastern upper course, eastward turn and subsequent east-to-southeast valley correspond to the Mineurs corridor in the thesis study-area and survey-segment figures. Figure23 differentiates Haute Mineurs and Basse Mineurs survey reaches while depicting their connecting river. The reserve map independently labels Ruisseau des Mineurs within its management territory. These observations support the named core corridor without assigning its name to the unresolved opening.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The Mineurs arrives from the west and joins the southern Lac branch; the combined course then turns northeast past the separate Échouement tributary. Figure23 and the thesis field-site prose establish these separate tributaries and their joins. The selected path follows the Mineurs side into this junction and does not traverse Lac Huard.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The selected eastward branch beyond the Échouement junction corresponds to Branche du Lac and reaches the northern Cascapédia branch before the main river turns south. The thesis figures depict this chain and distinguish the lake-fed northern Saumon branch from the selected western Mineurs approach. The2023 canoe-survey prose separately describes the Branche du Lac-to-Cascapédia descent, without supplying map-pixel evidence.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The southward main-river corridor below the branches and past the separate Square Forks drainage corresponds to the Cascapédia shown in the thesis study-area and survey-location maps. No lake, reservoir or glacier crossing is inserted into this selected main-river section. This is ordinary corridor correspondence, not a current bank or flow survey.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The thesis watershed/site maps continue the same main river southeast toward Cascapédia-Saint-Jules and New Richmond. Together with the river manager’s explicit geographic description and the2023 field-descent prose, they support the selected lower main-river approach at ordinary regional scale. Fine bank geometry and every island-side channel are not claimed from these generalized figures.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The sources explicitly identify the Cascapédia discharge to Baie des Chaleurs and the canoe route ending near Route132 at New Richmond. The selected terminal lies in this lower river/estuarine setting. However, the actually inspected regional figures do not separately resolve the selected final channel against nearby estuarine waterways; the Society leaflet map pixels were unavailable and the canoe-guide borrowed topographic panels were excluded. The terminal through-link therefore remains material-pending.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The original municipal drainage network depicts the selected southern feeder, its short eastward opening and its continuation toward the northeast. Nearby western drainage labels are not transferred to this feeder. The opening and intervening junctions are covered at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.role: Chosen west-to-east headward opening and first northeastern continuation

correspondence.finding: The municipal original continuously depicts the northeastward and then northward feeder through the forested interior, including the tributary junctions and the reach followed by the mapped conservation-area boundary. It continues toward the Pedra Sumurã and Flama setting without a missing selected through-link. No independent name is established for the full initial feeder.
correspondence.role: Long northward feeder and its small lateral tributary joins

correspondence.finding: The original map joins the northward feeder to the west-originating river near Pedra Sumurã and Flama, then depicts the selected northeastward and eastward turn. Both sides of the stage-3/stage-2 boundary are present. The separately described Calçoene headwaters near Lourenço are not substituted for the chosen southern opening.
correspondence.role: Selected northern approach, western receiving-river junction and eastward turn

correspondence.finding: The original depicts a continuous meandering river east from Flama, through the broad southward bend and toward the BR-156/Calçoene corridor. The selected lower turn connects into the wider mapped channel. Generalized stored segments cut some small meanders, but the selected corridor and its intermediate connections remain identifiable. No required lake, reservoir or managed interbasin passage is depicted along this selected interval.
correspondence.role: Eastward river, broad bend and approach to the lower northward reach

correspondence.finding: The municipal original connects the incoming eastward course through the northward reach by Cortical, Boa Esperança and Santa Cruz to Calçoene town. This covers the cross-fragment join and the stored town-area bend at ordinary corridor scale. The park plan independently links the named river, road crossing and town, and records tidal influence reaching the town. Exact present tidal limits or travel times are not inferred.
correspondence.role: Stage-2/stage-1 continuation, northward lower river and Calçoene town

correspondence.finding: The original depicts the connected lower meanders past the Minerva setting and the widening estuarine channel toward Nazaré and the Atlantic. The stored endpoint remains inside this widened river-mouth channel, short of the mapped open-ocean coastline; the underlying source endpoint is farther upstream in the last meander. The terminal extension stays in the same estuarine setting. No unshown wetland shortcut, separate lake passage or managed connector is needed to establish the selected continuation.
correspondence.role: Lower eastward meanders, widened tidal channel and actual selected endpoint

correspondence.component_scope: Southern opening and first northward reach
correspondence.finding: The regional thesis distinguishes several neighboring north-draining streams. It does not unambiguously identify this selected starting reach or its first through-link. No nearby named headwater is substituted.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.component_scope: Long northeast and northward interior corridor
correspondence.finding: The broad basin maps provide regional stream and settlement context, but they do not securely match the chosen corridor and all intermediate joins. A same-basin relationship is insufficient for component naming.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest turn and approach to the lake district
correspondence.finding: The thesis places the named regional inflows in the Alsina lake district. It does not establish the particular northwest approach or the selected transition to the following westward sequence.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lowland sequence and actual final terminal
correspondence.finding: The source documents regional lake interconnection and historical channel works. Those facts do not prove this selected westward passage, any intervening wetland or managed link, or the actual final terminal. Neither Laguna Alsina nor a neighboring lake is substituted for the stored end.
correspondence.role: mainstem

correspondence.finding: The eastern Tehery Lake sheet shows the chosen small pond/feeder approach joining a narrow waterbody, followed by a southwestward succession of short blue channels and small lakes. The western bend and subsequent southeastward return connect within this same depicted feeder. Adjacent northern and eastern waters are distinguishable; the selected beginning is not assigned the name of a nearby larger lake.
correspondence.role: Chosen northern opening, first pond/lake joins and western bend

correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues through elongated unnamed waters and short connecting channels, with the westward bend, southeastward return, lateral inflows and subsequent southern narrowing depicted continuously. The broad gray and colored thematic boundaries were distinguished from the underlying blue hydrography.
correspondence.role: Upper southward descent through narrow lakes and intervening joins

correspondence.finding: An unnamed mapped river follows the selected southward and eastward turns. The meanders, small widenings and incoming western/eastern channels connect into the northern lake approach. The nearby separately drawn lake and tributary labels are not transferred to the selected river.
correspondence.role: Middle river, tributary junctions and lake approach

correspondence.finding: The river broadens into connected multi-armed waters that lead south into the lake explicitly labelled Fehet Lake. The selected north-to-south passage and southeastern arm are continuously depicted at the map scale; the straight modeled portions do not imply surveyed crossings of individual banks or islands. Fehet Lake is a lake-component name, not an established whole-river hydronym.
correspondence.role: Northern multi-armed waterbody connection, Fehet Lake passage and southeastern arm

correspondence.finding: A blue connection leaves the southeastern Fehet Lake arm and leads through successive smaller lakes and narrow channels. The selected southern sequence, bends and lateral inflows remain readable beneath the red wildlife-theme overprint. These are connected mapped lake/river passages, not continuity inferred from neighboring lake names.
correspondence.role: Southeastern lake outlet, short channels and intervening unnamed lakes

correspondence.finding: The southward succession reaches the elongated lower lake that straddles the two sheets. Both original sheets depict the same lake shape and southern outlet setting, resolving the selected cross-sheet transfer and its intervening joins.
correspondence.role: Lower elongated lake and Tehery/Gibson sheet-boundary transfer

correspondence.finding: The northeastern Gibson Lake sheet continues the selected southward river from the boundary lake through connected narrows and widenings. Rapids are marked along the same corridor, and lateral streams remain distinct from the selected through-route.
correspondence.role: Lower river narrows, lake widenings and rapids

correspondence.finding: The route passes along the connected lower lake/river corridor and continues south through the mapped rapids and narrow waters. The larger western lake arm and the downstream connection are depicted together; the selected straight portion is treated as ordinary corridor generalization rather than exact bank alignment.
correspondence.role: Lower lake passage and final southward approach

correspondence.finding: The final connected channel and small lower widening reach the north side of Chesterfield Inlet in the West Point–Farther Hope Point setting. The original shows the receiving coastal water and the channel-to-inlet connection directly. The final modeled position is not treated as a surveyed tidal limit or present shoreline.
correspondence.role: Final channel and actual receiving-water connection
